newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY LEAGUE - Jones may be fit for S. Africa - Henry.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE - Jones may be fit for S. Africa - Henry.

text.p: LONDON, Feb 16 - All Black loose forward Michael Jones could be joining Auckland Blues for the South African leg of their rugby tour starting next month, NZPA reported on Monday (NZT).
The Blues are currently in Britain in the middle of a three-match mini-tour, which continues against glamour English club Harlequins on Tuesday.
Jones, the All Black blindside flanker, was a late withdrawal from the Blues squad because of minor knee surgery.
But coach Graham Henry said Jones is likely to join the team in South Africa, where they open their Super 12 campaign against Northern Transvaal on March 1.
"We spoke to Michael yesterday and things seem reasonably positive," Henry told NZPA.
"All things going well both he and Zinzan Brooke should join us in South Africa."
Brooke was another to opt out of the European tour, citing tiredness.
The Blues will field a near full-strength side for the match against London club Harlequins on Tuesday.
Of the team on the European tour, All Black captain Sean Fitzpatrick will be the only leading player not in the starting 15.
Auckland field 11 internationals against Harlequins, who are currently leading the English first division.
All Black prop Olo Brown will captain the side.

One of the glamour clubs of British rugby, Harlequins feature current Ireland captain Jim Staples, former England captain Will Carling, England vice-captain Jason Leonard and French goalkicking ace Thierry Lacroix among their host of stars.

After their comfortable 60-point win over Bristol on Thursday, Auckland will find Harlequins much tougher opponents, something reflected in their full-contact training session and intense scrumming practice today at the Stoop Memorial Ground, Harlequins' home in the shadow of the Twickenham international stadium.
Blues coach Graham Henry maintains, though, that the Harlequins game is just another build-up match to their Super 12 campaign.
"We're still not sure what our top combination is going to be," Henry added.
"But things are going fairly well. We're pretty happy after Tuesday, the attitude was good and the intensity level was good.
"If you had said we would play that well before Thursday I would have been happy.

"This next match is obviously one we also want to win, but more importantly we want to play well. A lot of guys here are still finding their feet, getting used body contact and being knocked around again.
"For us the most important match is coming on March 1."

Team: Adrian Cashmore, Joeli Vidiri, Eroni Clarke, Brian Lima, Lee Stensness, Carlos Spencer, Junior Tonu'u, Charles Riechelmann, Mark Carter, Robin Brooke, Richard Fromont, Leo Lafalii, Olo Brown (c), Andrew Roose, Orcades Crawford.
